title: Counting Missing Babies in Tanzania
subtitle: How well does Tanzania's health system count newborn deaths?
authors: Shabani J, Salim N, Malla L, Cross JH, Penzias RE, Victor A, et al.
one_line_summary: Tanzania's routine health system records only a fraction of the newborn deaths that surveys say are really happening.
cover_stat: 5.9 vs 24 per 1,000: the death rate the system reports, next to what national surveys find

title: Quality of Maternal & Child Health Services in Tanzania
subtitle: What a 2,583-facility star-rating review reveals about primary healthcare
authors: Kinyenje ES, Degeh MM, Hokororo JC, Mwaisengela SM, Ngowi RR, et al.
one_line_summary: Only about 1 in 10 primary health facilities in Tanzania met the quality standard for maternal and child health care.
cover_stat: Only about 1 in 10 facilities meet the maternal and child health quality standard

title: Hospital Maternal Mortality in Tanzania
subtitle: What ten years of records from 34 hospitals reveal about why mothers die
authors: Bwana VM, Rumisha SF, Mremi IR, Lyimo EP, Mboera LEG
one_line_summary: Across 34 public hospitals over 2006-2015, 1,987 women died from pregnancy or childbirth - most from eclampsia, bleeding and infection.
cover_stat: 1,987 maternal deaths in ten years, most from causes good emergency care can prevent

title: Severe Maternal Outcomes in Tanzania
subtitle: The deaths and the near-deaths at one hospital, and what they reveal
authors: Lilungulu A, Bintabara D, Mujungu S, Chiwanga E, Chetto P, Nassoro M
one_line_summary: Among 140 women with life-threatening pregnancy complications at a Dodoma hospital, 16 died and 124 nearly did - about eight near-misses for every death.
cover_stat: For every mother who died, nearly eight others came close
